## Paper

Scalable Evaluation of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Melting Pot

## World

resource_island

## Institution

Cross-world social-dilemma benchmark discipline.

## Agent type

Multi-agent RL agents evaluated across tasks.

## Theoretical benchmark

Generalization and robustness require held-out tasks/populations, not only in-distribution performance.

## Learning setup

Multiple social dilemma scenarios with train/test variation and agent-population evaluation.

## Metrics

Generalization, robustness, welfare, cooperation, exploitation, held-out scenario performance.

## Main result

Melting Pot reveals weaknesses in MARL algorithms not apparent from training performance alone; demonstrates how generalization to novel situations is critical for evaluating multi-agent reinforcement learning

## What they prove

The paper provides a benchmark/evaluation argument rather than a formal guarantee for this repo's purposes: MARL evaluation should test social generalization and robustness, not only in-distribution training performance.

## What they only simulate

Social generalization, resource sharing, and social dilemmas; cross-world synthesis and future held-out institution/world variants

## What they do NOT test

General social robustness from in-distribution training alone

## What we need to reproduce

Do not claim general social robustness from in-distribution training alone; use cross-world synthesis and future held-out variants.

## How our project differs

The benchmark suite is much broader. This repo has fewer worlds but uses explicit economic institutions and classical benchmarks.

## Implementation obligations

Cross-world synthesis; mechanism taxonomy; held-out variants as future work; no overclaim from one-world success.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

Cross-world synthesis outputs; future held-out institution/world variants.

## Failure modes to audit

Five worlds reported as five isolated tables; no synthesis; generalization claims without held-out tests.

## Project code comparison

Compare Scalable Evaluation of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Melting Pot to build_cross_world_synthesis.py outputs. The repo can become benchmark-like only if the synthesis, not just world count, is thesis-facing.
